distractor_rationales: airtight - having no gaps or loopholes ('an airtight alibi'); the endless quarrels over how to read its clauses show it was not airtight
balanced - fair to both sides ('a balanced diet'); nothing in the sentence concerns fairness, and fairness is not what the 'Although ... torn up' contrast sets up

academic - of theoretical interest only, or scholarly ('a purely academic question'); the quarrels over its clauses may sound scholarly, but the 'Although ... torn up within a decade' contrast asks how long it lasted, and a treaty no one would replace mattered in practice

clue_type: two-step cause: doctors chose which patients to enroll and picked those they expected to do well (fact) -> the samples were skewed from the start (inference) -> bias; 'honest statistics' rules out a deliberate agenda

distractor_rationales: agenda - a plan or hidden purpose ('a political agenda'); the doctors chose 'quite naturally' and the statistics were honest, so there was no scheme
antipathy - a strong dislike ('an antipathy to crowds'); the doctors picked patients out of hope for their recovery, not dislike of anyone, and nothing describes hostility
ailment - an illness ('a minor ailment'); the defect described is in how patients were chosen, not in any disease
